fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. God says, “You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.” (Exodus 20:23) That comes right after He reminds them that He has spoken to them from heaven. People can shape silver and gold into something shiny, but it's still just metal that somebody made.

That's it. God says, “Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.” (Exodus 23:8) Two things named there: it blinds those who see, and it twists the words of the righteous. Somebody who sees the situation clearly takes the bribe, and suddenly they can't see it anymore. That's why God says to stay away from it.

Right. God says they eat unleavened bread for seven days in the month of Abib “…because that was the month you came out of Egypt.” (Exodus 23:15) Every year, the bread on the table tells them what happened to them that month. I can't even remember what I ate last Tuesday, and they get a whole feast to help them remember the day they walked out of Egypt.

The law isn't given as the reason here, friend. God says they eat unleavened bread in Abib “…because that was the month you came out of Egypt.” (Exodus 23:15) The reason He gives is the leaving. The feast keeps pointing them back to the month they came out.

Leftovers aren't what God asks for, friend. He says, “Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.” (Exodus 23:19) Think of it like a guest coming to your house. You wouldn't hand them whatever you found at the back of the cabinet and call it a gift. You'd set out your best. God asks for the best of the firstfruits.
